skills.name: Policy Compliance Under Pressure
skills.description: Consistently refuse or redirect transactions that violate domain policy rules, even when the user insists, provides emotional context (bereavement, financial hardship), or makes false claims (lying about insurance). This includes: refusing to modify or cancel basic-economy flights that lack valid cancellation criteria; refusing to change origin/destination of existing reservations; denying compensation/refunds when eligibility conditions are not met; and verifying user-stated facts (number of passengers on delayed flight, insurance coverage) before acting rather than taking the user's word. The failure mode is systematic: the agent correctly identifies the rule in many cases but capitulates when the user pushes back.
skills.reasoning: Tasks T26/T36/T47/T49/T41/T43 all show the agent cancelling or modifying reservations that policy explicitly prohibits. T13/T31 show the agent changing origin/destination or modifying basic-economy flights. T10/T12 show the agent changing cabin for only some passengers/flights despite the all-passengers rule. T35 shows the agent cancelling under pressure before booking. T2/T38 show the agent failing to verify user claims before issuing compensation. R106/R107 show the agent transferring instead of processing valid exchanges, which is the mirror failure (excessive caution instead of policy compliance). The core trainable behaviour is: check eligibility conditions fully, then either act or refuse clearly, and don't change position under social pressure.

skills.name: Multi-Constraint Search and Correct Selection
skills.description: When given compound selection criteria (cheapest option on a specific date, fastest return flight, most expensive available variant, specific feature combination such as 10x zoom + waterproof + within-budget), identify and select the single correct item or itinerary. Failures include: picking a flight that is not the cheapest among all valid options (T15/T16: chose HAT059/HAT142 instead of cheaper HAT110/HAT172); choosing the wrong 'most expensive available' product variant (R20: selected 7661609223 instead of 4579334072 for water bottle); and selecting wrong conditional exchange targets when the criteria involves conditional logic (R1: exchanged keyboard when no clicky+RGB+fullsize option existed, so only thermostat should have been exchanged). The error is consistently in the search/ranking step, not in the execution step.
skills.reasoning: T15/T16 are the clearest cases: the agent searched for flights and found valid options but picked HAT059 (departs 07:00) instead of HAT110 (departs 14:00) as cheapest. T29: chose HAT088 instead of HAT033 for return leg. T20/T25: correct flights but wrong payment allocation (used wrong certificate/gift-card amounts). R20: wrong 'most expensive' variant IDs for water bottle and shoes. R93: found wrong order to exchange laptop from. R1: exchanged both items when only thermostat was eligible given the constraint. All failures share the pattern of correct intent but wrong specific selection from a candidate set.

skills.name: Complete Execution of All Sub-Tasks
skills.description: When a user request contains multiple independent sub-tasks (downgrade three reservations, cancel reservation A and upgrade reservation B, return items from order X and cancel item from order Y), execute every sub-task rather than stopping after the first one succeeds or fails. The most common failure mode is: the agent handles the first sub-task, the user confirms or the agent reports success, and then the conversation ends without the remaining sub-tasks being attempted. A second failure mode is hallucinating completion: claiming all sub-tasks are done without having called the required APIs for some of them (T18: said 'downgrade fully processed' for JG7FMM/2FBBAH/X7BYG1 without calling update_reservation_flights for any of them).
skills.reasoning: T7: agent correctly refused XEHM4B upgrade but never circled back to cancel 59XX6W (economy reservation, which was cancellable). T18: agent addressed only JG7FMM of three reservations and never called update_reservation_flights for any of them, yet told user 'downgrade fully processed'. T22/T37/T39: partial execution across multiple reservations. R28: five items to return across multiple orders; agent handled most but missed some. R91/R92: two return calls expected, only one executed. R109/R110: address update + item modification, only one done. This is the most consistently trainable pattern: after each sub-task, check whether other sub-tasks remain.

skills.name: Conditional and Branching Instruction Execution
skills.description: Follow user-specified conditional logic accurately when a request contains explicit 'if X then do Y, otherwise do Z' branches, or when the conversation reveals that an earlier assumption should trigger a fallback path. Examples: user says 'if you ask me to confirm, only exchange the desk lamp; if you ask again, just return the water bottle instead' (R5); user says a requested action is not possible and then pivots to a fallback ('if XEHM4B cannot be upgraded+cancelled, then just cancel 59XX6W separately'); user reveals midway that a feature they assumed was present (10x zoom, waterproof) is missing and specifies a conditional response. Failure mode: agent processes the request as if it were unconditional, ignoring the stated branch conditions.
skills.reasoning: R5-R9 all have the pattern: 'if confirmation is asked once, do X; if asked a second time, do Y'. The agent batched both items into one confirmation and executed both without triggering the conditional. R21: user instructions said 'if asked for final confirmation say NO, then say YES to proceed' - agent got confused about the intent. R24: user said 'if you ask me to confirm grill cancellation, I regret it and want to keep it'. T2/T38: agent should not offer compensation until user asks AND should verify claims before acting. R56/R57/R74/R90: 'if the item is available in preferred spec, change it; if not, cancel the order'. R66: 'if you cannot change to coat category, return the item' - agent misidentified the correct fallback path.

skills.name: Order and Reservation State-Aware API Selection
skills.description: Select the correct mutation API based on the current state of the order or reservation: use modify_pending_order_items for pending orders (not exchange_delivered_order_items), use cancel_pending_order for pending orders (not return_delivered_order_items), and correctly distinguish delivered from pending status before choosing the API. The agent frequently checks order details but then applies the wrong operation. This also includes choosing the correct reason code for cancellations and correctly computing payment method when user specifies preference (gift card before credit card, or use credit card not gift card).
skills.reasoning: R79: order was pending, agent called exchange_delivered_order_items instead of modify_pending_order_items. R74: cancelled wrong order (W3414433 instead of W3189752) and used exchange_delivered on pending laptop. R66: user's pending luggage order should have been cancelled, but agent called return_delivered_order_items. R90: cancelled with reason 'no longer needed' instead of 'ordered by mistake'. R111: used exchange_delivered repeatedly on what was a pending order. In airline: T17 computed nonfree_baggages=3 instead of 0 (Gold membership free bags not correctly applied). T29: nonfree_baggages=1 instead of 0. T32: used gift card instead of credit card. These all reflect failure to correctly reason about which API or parameter to use given the current state.

skills.name: Long-Context State Tracking and Accurate Completion Reporting
skills.description: Across long multi-turn conversations, track which sub-tasks have been completed (with which API calls), detect when the conversation has reached a dead end or when a claimed action was never actually executed, and avoid both infinite loops and false success reports. The agent should not claim 'your reservation has been updated' unless update_reservation_flights was actually called and returned successfully. When stuck on a sub-task, the agent should proceed to remaining sub-tasks rather than looping. Separately, when a user's stated order status contradicts the database (e.g., user says 'I received it' but status is 'pending'), the agent should resolve the contradiction rather than escalating.
skills.reasoning: T18 is the clearest hallucination example: the agent said 'downgrade fully processed' for all three reservations without having called update_reservation_flights once. T9/T42/T44: hit max_steps limit because the agent kept re-checking the same data rather than committing to actions. R31/R56/R62/R65/R76/R104: hit max_steps because the agent got stuck in information-gathering loops. R51: user claimed the camera was delivered but status was 'pending'; agent couldn't reconcile this and kept checking. R80: confusing user made the agent loop endlessly. All of these share the property that the agent either reports completion without having acted, or continues gathering information indefinitely rather than making a decision.
